doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Keppard compared with Louis Armstrong and Joe Oliver
summary: Taylor says Keppard improvised more and was Chicago's favourite before Louis rose, and compares his breaks and style with Oliver's.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: He recorded with Doc Cook too on his Marlick band. But he didn't do a lot of recording. You told me he did record with some of your small groups all the time. Yeah, small groups. You told him on that pile. Yeah.

Freddie could take just a little mediocre group and take that trumpet away where he could improvise and he could do things. I think that Louie was more of a stylist but he could do things. Freddie was. He seemed to have more tricks in store. More improvising. And more improvising.
Freddie was. How did they compare in that day? Did people think of Louie as being better? Or

Kepard as being better? Freddie was the favorite. And for Louie establishing. So Louie started, I think the first tune to make Louie was West End. And from then on, Louie came into his own and he started recording. But prior to this, Freddie Kepler had Chicago. And then Joe Sutler.
Joe Sutler you think could match pretty close to Kepler? Yeah, pretty close. And then Louie, Louie stepped up where we're both up. Yeah. He was recording. Strange that Sutler never got

properly recorded. No, he never did do very much. His work of the Edgar was on the ground. Yeah, the way they did with Kepard, the way they spotted him, was supposed to be a hokum man in those days, you call him. Outside man, hokum. He was ready to play with those hot dancers. He played down. And for the punch, then he called Freddie. He said Freddie would get up and take his jelly band. And he played over the band. And the band just went along and called him and some sort of a riff. And Boston they called it. But Freddie would just be outside man for the punch. And he'd take it on out. And he'd take it on out. And he'd go on out. Jimmy Wicks was a baby.
Well, Freddie. Well, I think Freddie had more stuff than Joe.
